old.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
old.hook: The city's oldest covered market, trading since 1615 and named for a vanished hospice whose orphaned children wore red. Half produce and flowers, half elbow-to-elbow lunch counters — a living market rather than a monument behind glass (listed historic since 1982).
old.text: The city's oldest covered market, trading since 1615 and named for a vanished hospice whose orphaned children wore red. Half produce and flowers, half elbow-to-elbow lunch counters — a living market rather than a monument behind glass (listed historic since 1982). Signal 39 rue de Bretagne, 3e (also enter via rue Charlot). Free. Tue-Sat 8:30-19:30, Sun 8:30-14:00, closed Monday. Come hungry and slightly before or after the 13:00 rush; small cash helps at the food stalls.

old.label: 6th (rue du Cherche-Midi)
old.text: Founded 1932; the two-kilo wood-fired sourdough miche is a Paris institution, not a fashion (Poilane; Wikipedia). Bread rather than pastry, but foundational. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Du Pain et des Idees
old.label: 10th (Canal Saint-Martin)
old.text: Christophe Vasseur, named a top Paris boulanger (2008); the chocolate-pistachio escargot is the pilgrimage pastry (TASTE; AFAR). Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Mori Yoshida
old.label: 7th (avenue de Breteuil)
old.text: One of the Japanese pastry chefs who reshaped Paris; opened 2013, winner of Le Meilleur Patissier: Les Professionnels 2018 — French classics with precise restraint (Sortiraparis; VisitParisRegion). Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Pierre Herme
old.label: 6th (Saint-Germain, rue Bonaparte)
old.text: The 'Picasso of pastry' (Vogue's Jeffrey Steingarten; La Liste); creator of the Ispahan — rose, lychee, raspberry — and a macaron benchmark. Open in Google Maps →

old.name: Cedric Grolet
old.label: 1st (Le Meurice / Opera)
old.text: Named World's Best Pastry Chef 2018 by the World's 50 Best; famous for trompe-l'oeil fruit desserts that look exactly like the fruit until you cut them open (World's 50 Best). Open in Google Maps →
